entries.name: Trampolina
entries.introduction: A colorful learning world for noticing, counting, matching, remembering and making sense of everyday patterns.
entries.purpose: Bring foundational ideas into approachable activities that children can explore with an adult or at their own pace.
entries.audience: Young children, parents and educators looking for short, adjustable learning experiences.
entries.age_guidance: Primarily designed around ages 2–6. Selected reasoning, mathematics and harder puzzles may also interest children aged 7–8. These are flexible starting suggestions, not age gates or developmental assessments.
entries.difficulty: Choose a small concept set or an easier board, then adjust the challenge. Several activities offer Smart progression and manual difficulty.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Notice colors, shapes, symbols and quantities.
Practise comparing, sorting, remembering and sequencing.
Build familiarity with learning through attempts, examples and feedback.
offers: Six connected laboratories: Colors, Numbers & Mathematics, Shapes, Letters, Memory & Perception, and Thinking & Logic.
Parent settings include language and voice selection, optional reminders, daily/session limits and a protected parent challenge.
Saved activities, learning reports and completion-based star rewards are implemented in the development app.

interaction.see: Illustrated learning worlds, large choices and child-friendly controls.
interaction.hear: English, Hebrew and Russian interfaces and four voice identities are configured. Full instructional narration is still missing; available praise/retry clips are separate.
interaction.do: Choose a laboratory, select concepts or difficulty, then follow that activity’s instructions.
interaction.feedback: Visual responses distinguish a completed task from an attempt; rewards are recorded for eligible completed activities.
interaction.progression: Children can repeat familiar tasks or move to more demanding boards without a universal age restriction.
interaction.help: Use an example, Help or replay where the activity provides it. The parent area uses a changing number challenge, not a persistent PIN.

tutorial.title: Choose a learning world
tutorial.text: Start with a topic the child recognizes or is curious about.

tutorial.title: Set a comfortable starting point
tutorial.text: Select fewer concepts or a gentler difficulty. An adult can demonstrate the first task.

tutorial.title: Explore one activity
tutorial.text: Read the activity guide together and let the child respond. Missing instructional audio is identified in the relevant guide.

tutorial.title: Keep control of the session
tutorial.text: Use Help, return to the category or stop when the child wishes. Parents may configure reminders and limits.

parent_tips: Treat the suggested ages as starting points; interest and familiarity matter.
Connect on-screen ideas to toys, clothing, food and everyday routines.
Star rewards are product feedback, not measures of ability or development.

entries.name: Colors
entries.introduction: Discover six familiar colors through visible examples, single matches, multiple matches and a later listening sequence.
entries.purpose: Offer repeated opportunities to distinguish a target color while the number and arrangement of choices change.
entries.audience: Children beginning color recognition, with an adult available for instructions and support.
entries.age_guidance: A gentle starting point around ages 2–3; multiple matches and listening tasks may suit older or more experienced children. Choose by readiness, not age alone.
entries.difficulty: Easy, Medium and Hard vary the number of visible choices. The two-choice listening stage always presents two options.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Compare a visible color with alternatives.
Find one or several cards sharing the target color.
Explore spoken-color recognition once approved recordings are supplied.
offers: Red, blue, yellow, green, orange and purple.
Five ordered stages: one visible match, all visible matches, listening Yes/No, listening with two cards and listening with all matches.
Visual examples can be replayed; completed tasks and skipped tasks are treated separately.

interaction.see: A target example and colored cards in the visual stages; no visible target in listening stages.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used.
interaction.do: Tap one match, select all matches or answer the listening question appropriate to the stage.
interaction.feedback: Correct selections remain recognized; an incorrect attempt allows another try.
interaction.progression: The journey advances through five stages, with adjustable choice density. Listening stages remain unavailable without their real target recording.
interaction.help: Replay the visible example or use Help. Audio-only tasks cannot reveal a visual substitute for the unheard target.

tutorial.title: Start with a visible example
tutorial.text: Look together at the target color before choosing a card.

tutorial.title: Find the right match
tutorial.text: Tap one matching card, or every matching card when the activity asks for all of them.

tutorial.title: Use the example again
tutorial.text: Replay the example if the child is unsure. Try again without rushing.

tutorial.title: Understand the listening boundary
tutorial.text: The later listening stages require approved recorded instructions. They are documented here but are currently unavailable in the app.

parent_tips: Name examples in the room after a visual match.
Start with fewer choices and avoid treating a mistake as a diagnosis.

entries.name: Numbers & Mathematics
entries.introduction: Meet numbers from 1 to 20, connect numerals with quantities and explore early addition and subtraction using visible groups of apples.
entries.purpose: Make the relationship between a written number, a counted set and a simple operation easier to explore.
entries.audience: Children beginning counting and numeral recognition, and children ready to try small-number arithmetic.
entries.age_guidance: Counting and recognition may be starting points around ages 3–6. Addition, subtraction and more demanding quantities may suit ages 4–8 with adult guidance. These are approximate suggestions.
entries.difficulty: Choose number groups 1–5, 6–10 or 11–20 for the curriculum. Arithmetic uses up to 5, up to 10 or both, with three difficulty levels.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Recognize and write familiar numerals.
Connect counting with a quantity and its numeral.
Explore combining and taking away concrete groups.
offers: A seven-stage number learning sequence: meet, trace, draw, recognize, count, compare groups and choose a numeral for a quantity.
Learn and Challenge use the selected number set.
Addition and Subtraction are distinct activities within Numbers World.

interaction.see: Large numerals, tracing guides, countable apples and quantity groups.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used.
interaction.do: Choose numerals, count visible objects, compare groups or write on the drawing surface. In arithmetic, watch the operation and choose the resulting quantity.
interaction.feedback: Visual feedback and retry opportunities follow answers; completed and assisted practice are distinguished.
interaction.progression: Learn introduces each selected number through several representations. Challenge revisits recognition and quantity; arithmetic adjusts support and difficulty.
interaction.help: Use the guide or Show me again. Arithmetic offers Another game, Back to Numbers World and supported stopping options.

tutorial.title: Select a number range
tutorial.text: Begin with a familiar range and select the numbers to practise.

tutorial.title: Choose Learn or Challenge
tutorial.text: Learn moves through several ways of meeting each number. Challenge revisits recognition and quantity choices.

tutorial.title: Try a representation
tutorial.text: Follow a trace, count the objects or match the requested quantity to its numeral.

tutorial.title: Explore arithmetic when ready
tutorial.text: Choose Addition or Subtraction and watch the apples move before answering.

parent_tips: Count actual objects alongside the screen.
Use a smaller selected range before increasing the number of choices.

entries.name: Shapes
entries.introduction: Explore shape names and outlines, find shapes in everyday objects and fit pieces into matching openings.
entries.purpose: Encourage comparison of an outline with the shape of a visible object or a matching space.
entries.audience: Children beginning shape recognition and children ready for more detailed matching boards.
entries.age_guidance: Basic shapes may be a starting point around ages 2–4. Object matching, larger boards and additional shapes may suit ages 3–6 and beyond according to familiarity.
entries.difficulty: Choose the starting shapes. Matching-hole difficulty can add more pieces and additional shapes; object matching progresses from one match to all relevant objects.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Recognize circle, square, triangle and rectangle.
Connect outlines with familiar objects.
Practise aligning a shape with its matching opening.
offers: Learn Shapes combines introduction, identification, matching and tracing.
Shapes and real-world objects moves from a single relevant object to multiple matches.
Shapes and matching holes uses drag-and-drop placement, with additional shapes on harder boards.

interaction.see: Clear shape examples, everyday objects or a board of shaped openings.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used.
interaction.do: Select the requested shape or object, follow an outline, or drag a piece into the corresponding opening.
interaction.feedback: Correct matches are retained and incorrect placements can be tried again.
interaction.progression: Focused practice uses selected shapes; Mixed practice uses the base set. Larger and more varied matching boards increase the challenge.
interaction.help: Use Help, replay or resume where provided. Choose a smaller set when the task feels too busy.

tutorial.title: Choose a shape experience
tutorial.text: Open Learn Shapes, real-world objects or matching holes.

tutorial.title: Compare before acting
tutorial.text: Look at the outline, object or opening, then select or place the match.

tutorial.title: Return for another type of practice

parent_tips: Look for circles, squares and rectangles among nearby objects.

entries.name: Letters
entries.introduction: Explore a selected alphabet through letter recognition, object or word associations, guided tracing and free drawing.
entries.purpose: Give children several ways to become familiar with the appearance of a letter and its place in a language.
entries.audience: Children curious about letters, with parent or educator support for language-specific names and pronunciation.
entries.age_guidance: Often a starting point around ages 4–6, with earlier or later exploration according to interest. This is not a reading-readiness assessment.
entries.difficulty: Select a small set of letters or the full alphabet. Learn provides a sequence of representations; Challenge revisits selected letters.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Notice the visual form of a letter.
Connect letters with the available language-specific examples.
Explore stroke direction and independent drawing.
offers: English, Hebrew and Russian alphabet selection.
Meet a letter, identify it, explore an association, follow the guide and draw independently.
Learn, Challenge and Resume use the selected alphabet and saved activity.

interaction.see: Large letter forms, relevant illustrated examples and a drawing surface.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used. Spoken letter-name availability must not be inferred from the interface language.
interaction.do: Identify a target letter, select an associated example or follow/draw its form.
interaction.feedback: Answers receive visual feedback; drawing support provides another attempt or a guide.
interaction.progression: The learning sequence moves from seeing to choosing and drawing; Challenge provides recognition questions from the selected set.
interaction.help: Replay the guide or use Help. An adult can provide the letter name while app recordings remain unavailable.

entries.name: Memory Game
entries.introduction: Remember where pictures are hidden and uncover matching pairs.
entries.purpose: Provide a concrete opportunity to recall locations after a brief preview.
entries.audience: Children who enjoy visual challenges, with adult support available.
entries.age_guidance: Gentler boards may suit ages 3–6; more demanding boards may also interest children aged 7–8. Use the child’s familiarity and preferred pace as the guide.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 2 pairs. Medium: 3–4 pairs. Hard: 5–6 pairs. Preview time is 3.6, 2.4 or 1.5 seconds respectively.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Notice picture locations during the preview.
Recall and compare two selected cards.
offers: A short preview shows the board before cards close.
Matched pairs remain found; Smart progression visits three levels, while manual practice uses one board.

interaction.see: Picture cards briefly face up, then a hidden board awaits matching.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used.
interaction.do: Tap two cards and compare the pictures; continue until every pair is matched.
interaction.feedback: Matching cards stay found. Different cards close again so the child can try another pair.
interaction.progression: Smart mode moves through Easy, Medium and Hard. Manual mode keeps the selected challenge for one board.
interaction.help: Help and preview replay preserve already-found matches while marking the round as assisted.

tutorial.title: Study the preview
tutorial.text: Look for pairs and notice where each picture sits before the cards close.

tutorial.title: Open two cards
tutorial.text: Tap one card and then another. Compare the pictures.

tutorial.title: Remember what was revealed
tutorial.text: Keep a successful pair or use the locations you just saw for the next attempt.

tutorial.title: Finish or replay
tutorial.text: Find every pair. Use Help/replay if needed, then return to the laboratory or another round.

parent_tips: Let the child explain a choice before giving the answer.
Use Help without treating assisted practice as failure.

entries.name: Letter Recognition

entries.name: Addition
entries.introduction: Watch apples join and choose how many there are afterward.
entries.purpose: Connect combining two groups with a small-number equation.
entries.audience: Children familiar with counting small groups, with adult support for the operation.
entries.age_guidance: Often a starting point around ages 4–6; may also suit ages 7–8 practising early arithmetic. Familiarity with the chosen quantities matters more than age.
entries.difficulty: Choose up to 5, up to 10 or both. Three levels vary the answer choices and amount of initial demonstration.
entries.status: Implemented in the mobile development app; presented here as an information guide. Public release availability has not been announced.
objectives: Follow a visible change in a quantity.
Connect the resulting group with its numeral.
offers: A dedicated activity within Numbers World.
The existing apples animation, Show me again help and supported ending options are preserved.

interaction.see: Apples joining into a combined group, an equation and numeral choices.
interaction.hear: The visual activity is implemented in the development app. Full instructional recordings are not yet available; existing praise and retry clips are separate. No substitute voice or language is used. The established hint can use an existing support phrase; this does not imply full arithmetic narration.
interaction.do: Watch the operation, count the resulting group and select its numeral.
interaction.feedback: A correct answer is shown with the completed equation. A mismatch allows retrying or replaying support.
interaction.progression: Manual practice works toward four independent successes; Smart progression considers performance at harder levels. Assisted completion remains a valid supported ending.
interaction.help: Show me again replays the existing visual help. Another game, Back to Numbers World, Finish together and Finish for today are available in the relevant states.

tutorial.title: Replay when needed
tutorial.text: Choose Show me again to revisit the established demonstration.

tutorial.title: Finish comfortably
tutorial.text: Continue the short run or use the supported ending and return to Numbers World.
